Short-term losses first reduce short-term gains, while long-term losses first reduce long-term gains. If a net loss remains in one category, it reduces any net gain in the other category. When your total capital losses exceed total capital gains, the allowable deduction against other income is the lesser of your total net loss or $3,000. For married individuals filing separately, the annual statutory limit is $1,500. Any remaining net loss carries forward to the next year as if you incurred it then, continuing indefinitely until completely used up. This connects to how tax loss harvesting works . Short-term losses offset short-term gains, and long-term losses offset long-term gains, before net balances cross over.
